meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Civil Law (Romano-Germanic tradition) with cantonal administrative overlay and federal statutory corporate law
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Switzerland–Germany Double Taxation Agreement (1971, as amended)
Switzerland–United States Double Taxation Agreement (1996, as amended by Protocol of 23 September 2009)
EFTA Convention and Switzerland's EFTA free-trade agreement network

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Swiss Code of Obligations (SR 220) Arts. 620–763, as revised effective 1 January 2023; Art. 626 No. 1 (registered office and articles of association); Art. 632 (minimum paid-in share capital CHF 50,000); Art. 933b et seq. (central register of beneficial owners, UBO register) together with Arts. 58–63 of the Commercial Register Ordinance (HRegV; SR 221.411); Federal Act on Combating Money Laundering and Terrorist Financing (AMLA/GwG) of 10 October 1997 (SR 955.0) as amended, in particular Arts. 2–8; FINMA Circular 2016/07 (prevention of money laundering, PEP diligence) and FINMA Circular 2019/02 (blockchain/DLT business models); Federal Act on Embargoes (EmbG; SR 946.231) and the consolidated sanctions enforcement regime of the State Secretariat for Economic Affairs (SECO).

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified copy of passport or national identity card of each individual founder, director and authorised signatory
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: National passport or identity authority of the country of origin; notarisation by a local notary
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (if origin state is an HCCH 1961 contracting party) otherwise Swiss Consular Legalization of the notary's signature

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Extract from the foreign commercial register / certificate of good standing for any corporate founder or sole shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent commercial registry authority of the corporate founder's home jurisdiction
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or Swiss Consular Legalization

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: National police or criminal records authority of the state of former residence
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or Swiss Consular Legalization

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Debt enforcement register excerpt (Betreibungsauskunft) for Swiss-resident founders and directors
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Cantonal debt enforcement office (Betreibungsamt) of the place of residence
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Direct Swiss issuance; no apostille required

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Power of attorney granted to the incorporation fiduciary or attorney-at-law
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Founders, executed before a notary in Switzerland or abroad

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory risk-based screening of all founders, directors and beneficial owners against the consolidated SECO sanctions database (State Secretariat for Economic Affairs) implementing UN Security Council resolutions and EU restrictive measures adopted by Switzerland under the Federal Act on Embargoes (SR 946.231); statutory PEP identification under AMLA Art. 3, enhanced due diligence under AMLA Arts. 6, and FINMA Circular 2016/07 standards; supplementary screening against the OFAC SDN and Consolidated Non-SDN lists as best practice for US-dollar and US-person exposure; for USDC crypto payment rails, originator and beneficiary verification is aligned with FINMA Circular 2019/02 and FATF Recommendation 16 (travel rule) guidance; the incorporation fiduciary and the opening Swiss bank perform this screening and retain written records for at least 10 years under AMLA-like standards; the ISIC 6201 AI/LLM API platform itself is not an AMLA-regulated intermediary unless it performs payment intermediation, digital-asset custody or exchange services, in which case a FINMA VASP/PSP licence would be triggered.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Zefix – Central Business Name Index of the Swiss Federal Commercial Register Office (www.zefix.ch); name clearance and registration are effected through the competent Cantonal Commercial Register Office (Handelsregisteramt) of the seat canton
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Pursuant to Art. 950 OR and Arts. 29–30 HRegV, the company name must not be misleading and must contain the legal-form suffix 'Aktiengesellschaft' or the abbreviation 'AG' (French 'Société Anonyme'/'SA'; Italian 'Società Anonima'/'SA'); only Latin characters are admissible in the registered name, so non-Latin scripts must be transliterated into a Swiss national language (German, French, Italian or Romansh); the name must be clearly distinguishable in Switzerland from all existing registered names and protected trademarks under Art. 951 OR and must accurately describe the AI/LLM API activity, with internationally comprehensible tokens (e.g., 'AI', 'LLM', 'API', 'Digital', 'Inference') permitted provided they are not deceptive.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: SWISS / SCHWEIZ / SUISSE / SVIZZERA and country or sovereign designations (require prior consent of the Federal Department of Justice via the Swiss Federal Institute of Intellectual Property)
EIDGENOSSENSCHAFT / CONFEDERATION / CONFEDERAZIONE / FEDERAL / BUND (official sovereign terminology, protected)
BANK / BANQUE / BANCA / KASSE (requires a FINMA banking licence)
INSURANCE / VERSICHERUNG / ASSURANCE (requires a FINMA insurance licence)
TRUST / TREUHAND / FIDUCIAIRE (where the name implies regulated fiduciary, trustee or wealth-management activity)
FOUNDATION / STIFTUNG / FONDATION (requires foundation supervisory authority consent)
FUND / FONDS (implying a collective investment scheme, requires FINMA authorisation)
National, cantonal and municipal coats of arms, heraldic emblems and official seals (Art. 950 para. 2 OR)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon receipt of a written rejection notice from the Cantonal Commercial Register Office, the applicant (or its notary) may, within 30 days of service, file a reasoned written request for reconsideration, offering a revised distinctive element or a narrowed name. If the rejection is confirmed, an administrative appeal may be lodged with the competent Cantonal Administrative Court within 30 days of the negative decision, in accordance with Art. 71 of the Federal Administrative Procedure Act (VwVG) and the applicable cantonal procedural law. A further appeal on federal-law grounds lies to the Federal Supreme Court (Bundesgericht) in Lausanne. In parallel, the applicant may immediately resubmit an amended name without awaiting the appeal. Name reservations may be extended once for an additional 30-day period upon written application prior to expiry, provided the constitutional documents are filed within the extended window, after which priority lapses.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: For the ISIC 6201 AI/LLM API platform, a pure 'virtual mailbox' or P.O. Box is not permissible as a registered office under Art. 626 No. 1 OR; however, professional domiciliation through a licensed corporate service provider maintaining physical premises in the seat canton (e.g., Zug or Zurich) is accepted and compliant, provided such provider accepts service of process and the company maintains full books and records accessible at the address; the registered office must also be consistent with the place of effective management for Swiss federal and cantonal tax domicile purposes.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low, estimated at approximately 5% per annum for a standard, non-licensed AI/LLM API platform using regulated payment rails; the risk rises to approximately 15–20% per annum if material USDC crypto-currency flows, high-density domiciliation addresses, or clients in FATF high-risk jurisdictions trigger enhanced supervisory attention, in which case immediate production of complete books and records at the registered office is required.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Pre-incorporation name clearance and preliminary name check (Vorabklärung) via Zefix and the Cantonal Commercial Register Office
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Cantonal administrative fee schedule (Gebührenverordnung), typically CHF 50–100; Zefix name search itself is free of charge

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Hague apostille / consular legalization of foreign corporate documents, identity documents, police clearances and powers of attorney (bundle of four origin documents)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Competent apostille authority of each country of origin and Swiss consular representation where applicable
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: HCCH 1961 apostille fees (approximately USD 10–100 per document) plus Swiss consular legalization fees (CHF 78–150 per document); estimated USD 150 per document

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Certified translations of foreign-language documents into the language of the seat canton (German, French or Italian)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark of USD 40–60 per certified 250-word page; estimated five to seven pages

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Notarial deed of incorporation and public deed certification (Art. 629 OR)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Notary public (Urkundsperson) of the seat canton
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Regulated cantonal notarial tariff; for CHF 100,000 nominal share capital, approximately CHF 1,200–2,000, scaled by share capital bands

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Swiss Commercial Register entry fee for the newly formed Aktiengesellschaft
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory cantonal register fee schedule; for a CHF 100,000 AG typically CHF 600–1,200 plus federal components

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Official publication of the formation in the Swiss Official Gazette of Commerce (SHAB)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Swiss Official Gazette of Commerce (SHAB), Federal Commercial Register Office
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory publication tariff per original formation entry, approximately CHF 300–700

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Blocked paid-in share capital on a FINMA-licensed Swiss bank account (minimum CHF 50,000; released to free cash after registration)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Company's own Swiss bank account (bank confirmation issued to the notary and register office)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory minimum capital requirement per Art. 632 OR - at least CHF 50,000 paid in; refundable company asset, not an expense

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Domiciliation and registered office service for the first year in the seat canton (Zug or Zurich corporate service provider)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Licensed Swiss domiciliation provider (administrative office / registered office service)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark of CHF 150–300 per month for licensed domiciliation service in Zug or Zurich

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Professional incorporation fees of the Swiss fiduciary or attorney-at-law (formation, notary coordination, commercial register filing, UBO notification, corporate documentation)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Swiss fiduciary or attorney-at-law engaged for formation
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark for a streamlined Swiss AG incorporation with UBO register notification and compliance preparation: CHF 3,000–5,000 (approximately USD 3,400–5,600); hourly rates CHF 300–500

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: AML/CFT screening and UBO compliance file assembly (PEP, sanctions and source-of-funds checks for founders, directors and beneficial owners)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Formation fiduciary in conjunction with commercial KYC database vendors
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Per-subject commercial KYC/database fees plus Swiss attorney time; consistent with AMLA Arts. 5–8 due diligence and FINMA Circular 2016/07

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Swiss Code of Obligations (Obligationenrecht, OR), Articles 620–761 (Aktiengesellschaft) and Article 640 (minimum capital); Swiss Registration Ordinance (Handelsregisterverordnung, HRegV)
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Cantonal Commercial Register Office (Handelsregisteramt / Office du registre du commerce)
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Public Deed of Incorporation (Statuten / Statuts) executed before a Swiss notary public
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: Minimum nominal share capital of CHF 100,000 subscribed in full; at least 20% of the nominal value of each share must be paid up, and the aggregate paid-up amount must be at least CHF 50,000, deposited into a bank escrow account (Sperrkonto) that is blocked until registration and released only to the company's management
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: At the inaugural board meeting of CH AG, held by way of circular resolution, the board unanimously: (1) confirmed the subscription and full payment of the shares in accordance with the deed of incorporation; (2) adopted the registered office at the statutory address in Switzerland and authorized the lease; (3) appointed [Name] as Chief Executive Officer with sole signature and [Name] as Board Chair with authority to open bank accounts; (4) instructed the CEO to file the incorporation application with the Commercial Register Office and to complete all licensing, occupational safety, and environmental formalities.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Prepare and Notarize the Deed of Incorporation and Articles of Association
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Swiss Notary Public (Cantonal Notary) in the canton of the registered office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the draft articles of association and shareholder resolutions to the notary. The notary verifies legal compliance, records the paid-up capital and share subscriptions, and authenticates the incorporation deed. Shareholders must sign personally or by written proxy.
required_dossiers: Shareholders' identification documents (passport/ID)
Draft articles of association (Statuten/Statuts)
Statement by shareholders on share subscriptions and paid-up capital
Power of attorney if a proxy signs
List of board members and auditors with information on their authority to sign
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary identifies defects in the articles, amend and re-execute the deed; if the deed is rejected after notarization, rectify the notarized deed and re-file within 30 days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Open Escrow Account and Deposit Paid-Up Capital
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Corporate bank in Switzerland licensed by FINMA (e.g. Swiss cantonal bank or commercial bank)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Provide the notarized deed and board resolution to the bank to open a blocked account in the name of the company in formation. Transfer the required paid-up capital from the shareholders (minimum CHF 50,000). Obtain a written escrow confirmation (Sperrkonto-Bestätigung) addressed to the Commercial Register Office.
required_dossiers: Notarized deed of incorporation and articles
Board resolution authorizing the account opening
Identity documents and beneficial ownership declaration of shareholders
Bank account application forms and compliance/aml declarations
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank refuses confirmation due to compliance questions, provide enhanced due diligence documentation; if the capital deposit is deficient, require shareholders to cure the shortfall and re-confirm the balance.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Submit Incorporation Application to the Commercial Register Office
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Cantonal Commercial Register Office (Handelsregisteramt / Office du registre du commerce)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the signed and notarized deed, the application form, and all supporting documents with the Commercial Register Office. The application may be submitted electronically via the e-register portal in most cantons. The office verifies capital, legal form, identity of officers, and compliance with the company name law.
required_dossiers: Notarized deed of incorporation
Commercial register application form (signed by authorized board members)
Escrow deposit confirmation (Sperrkonto-Bestätigung)
List of board members, CEO, and auditors
Declaration of authorized signatories (signature cards)
Notice of the registered office and its exact address
If applicable, audit confirmation / auditor nomination
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registry queries the application, respond in writing within the prescribed deadline (usually 10 days) by amending the deed or providing additional evidence; if the name is rejected, submit a new name reservation and update the articles.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Receive Commercial Register Extract and Legal Personality
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Cantonal Commercial Register Office and the Federal Commercial Register
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upon approval, the Commercial Register Office enters the company into the official register and publishes the relevant facts in the Swiss Official Gazette of Commerce (Schweizerisches Handelsamtsblatt, SHAB). The company obtains legal personality on the date of registration.
required_dossiers: Registry decision (provided by the registry)
Commercial register extract (Handelsregisterauszug / Extrait du registre du commerce)
Publication confirmation in SHAB
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registration is not published or the extract contains errors, file a request with the Commercial Register Office for correction; any third-party objection to the registration must be challenged in the cantonal supervisory authority.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Register for VAT, AHV/Social Insurance, and Accident Insurance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Federal Tax Administration (ESTV / FTA) for VAT and UID; cantonal tax office for corporate income tax; Swiss Compensation Office (ZAS/AHV) for social insurance; SUVA or private insurer for accident insurance
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the official registration forms to obtain (i) the business identification number (UID/IDE), (ii) VAT registration (by default CHF 100,000 annual turnover threshold), (iii) AHV employer number, and (iv) accident insurance registration. File electronically or by mail using the commercial register extract.
required_dossiers: Commercial register extract
Articles of association
Identification of directors and shareholders
Bank account details
AHV registration form
Employee declaration (if any)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the tax office raises questions, provide corrected corporate structure data; if the UID number is not issued within the SLA, escalate via the ESTV helpdesk; ensure all social insurance registrations are completed before hiring employees to avoid retroactive penalties.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Complete Work Premises and Physical Licensing Formalities
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Cantonal labour inspectorate; municipal trade/permitting office; cantonal building insurance; cantonal environmental agency
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: For administrative office premises used for AI and software operations, notify the local municipal administration about the business activity. Engage an occupational safety specialist if needed. Obtain fire safety confirmation and, if any structural alteration is required, obtain building permit clearance. For purely IT services no industrial operating permit is required.
required_dossiers: Lease contract or proof of enjoyment of premises
Floor plan and description of office use
Occupational safety and accident prevention declaration
Fire safety confirmation from the cantonal building insurance
Business notification form for the municipal/cantonal authorities
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the municipal notification is queried, update the use declaration and re-submit; if fire safety certification is missing, schedule an inspection with the cantonal fire prevention service and correct any deficiencies.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Cantonal Office of Economic Affairs (Amt für Wirtschaft / Office de l'économie) – generally not applicable; the managed office activity falls under free economic activity under the Swiss Federal Constitution (Art. 27 and 94)
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: No statutory operating license required for ISIC 6201 (generative AI and LLM API platform) under Swiss federal or cantonal law; commercial activity is only subject to ordinary business notification and municipal feepayment

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Federal Office for the Environment (FOEN / BAFU / UFAM)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt – administrative office use, no significant environmental impact; no formal EIA required under Annex 1 of the Environment Impact Assessment Ordinance (EIAO / UVPV)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No industrial wastewater, VOC, or hazardous-air emissions from the defined activity. Office facilities must comply with the cantonal waste disposal regulations, e-waste take-back obligations under the WEEE Ordinance, and OWAM / SWICO recycling standards. Any server room cooling condensate must be disposed of in accordance with local sewer discharge ordinances.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certification issued by the cantonal building insurance (Gebäudeversicherung / Établissement cantonal d'assurance) confirming the premises are suitable for office occupancy; structural load integrity declaration based on the building permit if any server racks exceed 5 kN/m²; workplace safety clearance from the cantonal labour inspectorate and, where applicable, SUVA confirming adherence to Art. 82 EGA (Ordonnance sur la prévention des accidents) and ventilation/lighting standards.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Swiss Federal Tax Administration (ESTV/FTA; official portal www.estv.admin.ch) with cantonal tax authorities for corporate income tax assessment at the registered-seat canton.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A Swiss AG automatically receives the Swiss business identifier (Unternehmens-Identifikationsnummer or UID) when entered in the Commercial Register. For VAT purposes, the AG must file an online registration to the ESTV under Art. 10 of the VAT Act (Loi sur la TVA/MWSTG) in order to obtain the VAT number (MWST/TVA-Nr) if taxable turnover exceeds CHF 100,000. Foreign entities seeking a Swiss presence first register a branch or subsidiary in the Commercial Register, triggering UID issuance, then apply for VAT and cantonal tax IDs through the same ESTV and cantonal channels.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation – The Swiss AG is a separate corporate tax subject, liable to federal corporate income tax, cantonal/communal profit and capital taxes, and Swiss withholding tax on distributions. No pass-through treatment is available.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No check-the-box regime exists under Swiss law. Statutory elections are limited to VAT group taxation (Art. 14 VAT Act) and federal tax group taxation ('Steuerliche Tragerschaft' / 'statut de groupe'), whereby qualifying Swiss group companies can elect to be taxed as a single federal profit tax unit. Hybrid mismatch elections are not available under Swiss domestic law.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value Added Tax (Swiss VAT / Taxe sur la valeur ajoutee / Mehrwertsteuer)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: CHF 100,000 annual taxable turnover from Swiss supplies, excluding VAT; foreign suppliers of digital services to Swiss private consumers may have registration obligations irrespective of turnover based on place-of-customer rules.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Switzerland does not operate real-time fiscal clearance, stamping, or mandatory government-API approval of invoices. Swiss QR-bill requirements govern payment documents. VAT compliance is carried through periodic returns filed via the ESTV secure eService portal, with electronic records accepted, but there is no continuous transaction-control clearance requirement.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Export of goods qualifies for 0% VAT when the goods are physically exported from Switzerland and proof of export is furnished. For the AI LLM API platform, offshore supplies of digital/database services to foreign business customers are outside Swiss VAT scope under place-of-supply rules, or qualify for zero-rating where the recipient is a non-Swiss business and documentary evidence of foreign establishment is retained. Services to Swiss private consumers do not qualify for export zero-rating.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (Ausfuhrschein / declaration via Swiss customs e-dec process)
Bill of Lading or Air Waybill (international transport evidence)
Inward Remittance Certificate or foreign bank credit statement (payment evidence)
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: ESTV audits zero-rated claims by matching export declarations, international transport documents, contracts and payment evidence. Unsupported or fraudulent zero-rating is reversed with reassessment, default interest, and administrative fines. Intentional VAT evasion carries criminal fines and possible imprisonment, with a 10-year limitation period for retrospective reassessment in tax evasion cases; the ordinary assessment period is generally 5 years. There is no statutory Swiss FX repatriation deadline, but the 180-day benchmark is applied administratively for payment reconciliation in export substantiation reviews.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Swiss National Bank (SNB) in conjunction with the State Secretariat for International Finance (SIF) for financial market policy, and FINMA for banking supervision and anti-money laundering oversight
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Switzerland operates a fully liberalized and convertible currency regime without distinction between capital and current account transactions; non-residents may freely hold Swiss francs and repatriate dividends, profits, royalties, and capital in any convertible currency. No prior authorization is required for profit remittance or capital returns, subject only to standard anti-money laundering documentary obligations imposed on Swiss banks. The Swiss franc is not subject to exchange controls, and there are no restrictions on foreign currency accounts, but the SNB retains statutory powers to impose temporary protective measures in extraordinary circumstances, including negative interest rates and mandatory reserve requirements, although such measures have historically targeted domestic liquidity rather than cross-border convertibility.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Switzerland imposes no statutory timeline for the surrender or repatriation of export proceeds and no mandatory conversion ratio into Swiss francs; exporters and digital service providers, including AI API platforms, are free to retain, reinvest, or convert foreign currency receivables in the open interbank market. Banking clients must nevertheless comply with the Swiss Code of Obligations and FINMA anti-money laundering directives regarding the identification of the economic background and the source of funds when routing export receipts through Swiss bank accounts, and any inward payment exceeding CHF 15,000 may trigger enhanced documentary scrutiny if the transaction appears unusual.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: UBS Switzerland AG (Zurich and Geneva offices)
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Account for cross-border receivables and trade disbursements

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Credit Suisse (UBS group entity, operating under FINMA license)
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account and Multi-currency Corporate Account
Operational Account and CHF clearing account
Capital Escrow Account and Wealth Management Treasury Account
Fintech-ready multi-currency account with digital onboarding

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: Medium. Offshore electronic money institutions (EMIs) and digital payment banks such as Stripe, Airwallex, or Revolut cannot operate a deposit-taking or payment account for a Swiss AG without obtaining a FINMA banking or fintech licence or establishing a Swiss branch, due to the Swiss Banking Act, the Financial Services Act (FinSA), and the Financial Institutions Act (FinIA). A Swiss-resident AI LLM API platform may use an offshore EMI solely as a payment-collection facilitator for inbound card and crypto settlements, provided the EMI is contractually exempt from acting as a Swiss-regulated payment intermediary and the main treasury settlement account remains with a Swiss FINMA-licensed bank. Cryptocurrency stablecoin rails (USDC) are viable only if routed through a FINMA-licensed crypto custody provider or Swiss-regulated securities firm to avoid to unlicensed third-party risk.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Swiss banks universally require a physical appearance by a controlling director, the beneficial owner, and, for AG structures, an authorized signatory for the first onboarding interview when establishing a high-touch corporate relationship. Remote opening is occasionally permitted via a video-identification process for simple operational accounts, but Swiss anti-money laundering regulation requires a comprehensive legal entity verification, an economic-background interview, and a detailed client-profile questionnaire; in practice, the final compliance approval for a Swiss AG with a Web3 or AI API treasury requires at least one on-site meeting at the bank's premises or a certified Swiss notary or legal counsel acting as the bank's introduction agent. Given the statutory requirement under the Swiss AML-Ordinance to identify the 'beneficial owner' of legal entities, the director(s) must also present the original passport, certified company excerpt (Handelsregisterauszug), articles of association, and—unless the company is listed—a signed declaration to the bank acknowledging the source of AI platform licensing revenues.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Crypto-related revenue inflows, especially stablecoin tokens such as USDC and merchant settlement from cryptocurrency processors
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: (1) FINMA-recognized blockchain analytics reports tracing each inbound USDC transfer to an identified third-party merchant or verified wallet; (2) pass-through payment agent agreement with a qualified crypto payment processor (e.g., a MiCA-licensed entity or a FINMA-compliant digital asset exchange) demonstrating that no anonymous counterparty is involved; (3) a liquidity-clearing path converting 100% of crypto-origin revenue into fiat via a regulated exchange or OTC desk before any transfer to the Swiss bank; (4) a written compliance policy approved by the board of directors addressing the travel rule, wallet screening, and sanction-frozen address filtering; (5) audited confirmation from an IP-backed AI platform demonstrating that each API token sale corresponds to a real identifiable enterprise customer under a standard commercial contract.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-risk jurisdiction beneficiary pattern or repetitive same-day inbound transfers from United States LLCs without tax transparency
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: (1) UBO registry excerpt of the counterparty corporate entity, or in the absence of a public registry, a notarized certificate of incorporation and tax residency certificate; (2) the relevant API licensing agreement with a defined pricing schedule proving genuine business delivery; (3) a consolidated invoice number of inbound remittances aligned with API token usage records; (4) a FATCA and CRS self-certification of the Swiss AG to demonstrate that cross-border payments do not mask tax evasion; (5) a bank-prescribed commercial questionnaire confirming that the Swiss AG has no office of substance in a tax-haven jurisdiction and that the Geneva/Zug operating premises are identifiable.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Third-party disbursement to foreign subcontractors or non-resident technology developers initiating unusual commission-like payments
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: (1) Written subcontracting or service agreements identifying the developer and the exact algorithm or infrastructure service delivered; (2) benchmark or invoice evidence of the fair-market value of such services; (3) a Swiss VAT/GST invoice if applicable; (4) an internal transfer-pricing memo in accordance with OECD principles to avoid profit-stripping characterization; (5) a business justification memo referencing the AI LLM API platform's procurement workflow.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Directors acting simultaneously as signatories for multiple freshly incorporated AG entities or holding residence outside of Switzerland
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: (1) Biographical statement and employment contract proving a substantive, professional directorship of the Swiss AG; (2) proof of accommodation in Switzerland (rent agreement or purchase deed) for at least-one director if residency is required; (3) tax clearance certificate from the director's home jurisdiction when relevant; (4) company organizational chart and decision-making protocol demonstrating that the board of the Swiss AG is not a nominee shell; (5) a written undertaking from the qualified Swiss accountant to maintain proper timeliness of accounts under Swiss law.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Projected high-volume API revenues disproportionate to the stated initial paid-in capital, triggering PEP or unexplained-wealth suspicion
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: (1) Audited five-year business plan and revenue model of the AI LLM API platform, including backend infrastructure contracts and enterprise deployment milestones; (2) signed subscription agreements or letters of intent from target US and EU customers; (3) intellectual property assignment records for the source code and proprietary AI models; (4) tax pre-approval or a transparent confirmation from a Swiss licensed auditor that the revenue expectations correspond to the company's actual corporate substance; (5) a clean-source-of-funds statement for the injected share capital and detailed trace of any third-party funding.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant wire transfer protocols for capital contribution into the Swiss AG require the funds to be routed from a bank account held in the name of the non-resident shareholder or its clearly disclosed holding vehicle. The wire must reference the purpose code 'KEH' or 'INVE' by internal bank practice, although Swiss law does not mandate a specific SWIFT purpose code; the mandatory narrative in the payment field should state 'Einlage Kapitalerhöhung' or 'Capital Contribution / CH-AG equity injection', accompanied by a board resolution approving the contribution and a notarised deed of increase in capital if applicable. The beneficiary account must be the Swiss AG's capital escrow account. Prior to execution, the bank must receive a signed source-of-funds letter from the shareholder, a copy of the passport or certificate of incorporation, the bank statement showing the shareholder's funds, and, where the contribution exceeds CHF 1 million, an audited confirmation of the economic background and the valuation of any monetary or non-monetary consideration. Payment can be made in CHF, USD, EUR, or any freely convertible currency; the receiving Swiss bank will convert to CHF only pursuant to a standing treasury instruction. Verification of the transaction is completed via the bank's sanction screening, adverse-media check, and a positive match of the shareholder name against the corporate register excerpt.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound trade settlements for the AI LLM API platform's supplier contracts, cloud infrastructure payments, and cross-border licensing royalties are executed through the Swiss Interbank Clearing (SIC) system for same-day domestic CHF payments, and through SWIFT MT103 for inbound/outbound cross-border fiat wires, typically via the corridor banking network of UBS, ZKB, or another Swiss clearing bank. For medium-value commercial transactions exceeding CHF 50,000, the Swiss bank may require a full narrative in the SWIFT field 70 to describe the contract invoice number, the underlying service, and the commercial purpose; invoices must be issued under Swiss VAT law, and Swiss withholding tax on royalties and licence fees (up to 4.4% or treaty-reduced) must be settled with the Swiss Federal Tax Administration before repatriation to foreign service providers. A documentary commercial letter of credit (UCP 600) is permissible for high-value infrastructure procurement outside Switzerland, but given the digital nature of AI API services, the standard practice is the use of irrevocable payment commitments under the bank's e-banking export collection module, combined with SWIFT MT950 balance reporting for liquidity forecasting. Cross-border disbursement in USDC or other stablecoins is not permitted through conventional SWIFT rails; such disbursements must be converted to CHF or USD via a FINMA-regulated crypto broker before leaving the Swiss banking circuit.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Plain-vanilla deliverable foreign exchange forwards between CHF, USD, EUR, and other freely convertible currencies executed under an ISDA Master Agreement or a Swiss bank's OTC derivative terms
Swiss franc exchange-traded futures and options cleared via Eurex for listed forward exposure management
Outright currency call and put options written by a FINMA-licensed bank providing asymmetric protection on USD-based API licensing revenue streams
Cross-currency interest rate swaps (if debt financing is introduced) to align interest payment mismatches between Swiss francs and US dollars

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) are lawful but only relevant for trading counterparties in restricted currencies; the Swiss franc itself is fully deliverable, so NDFs are not necessary and are not typically offered for CHF-based transactions
FX swaps for managing short-term treasury liquidity mismatches between foreign receivables and Swiss franc operating costs

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Federal, Cantonal and Communal Corporate Income Tax Return (tax declaration for the AG, including signed financial statements and capital tax schedule)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Swiss Federal Tax Administration (ESTV/FTA) and the Cantonal Income Tax Office having jurisdiction over the registered office
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: For calendar-year accounting, no later than 31 March of the following year; upon written request, ordinary extension to 30 September; for non-calendar-year companies, within 180 days after the balance-sheet date
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Default assessment and procedural fine for late filing; arrears interest at 5% per annum for cantonal taxes and up to 9.5% for federal taxes; aggravated non-compliance may lead to administrative enforcement and compulsory liquidation proceedings

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Value Added Tax (VAT) Return and payment declaration under the Swiss VAT Act
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Swiss Federal Tax Administration, Main Division VAT (ESTV/AFD)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Returns are due within 60 days following the expiry of each allocated VAT period (calendar quarter, half-year or annual term as assigned by ESTV); annual-declaration businesses file no later than 60 days after 31 December unless an extension is granted
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing triggers a default VAT assessment and arrears interest at 9.5% per annum; deliberate under-declaration can be prosecuted as tax evasion with fines of up to 30% of the evaded VAT amount and possible revocation of the right to deduct input VAT

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual General Assembly Minutes, Board Report and Statutory Financial Statements (approved balance sheet, profit-and-loss statement and notes where required)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Company shareholders’ general assembly (internal corporate organ); not filed with the Commercial Register unless the meeting gives rise to registrar-bound changes such as director resignation or auditor appointment
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Held within six months of the balance-sheet date; for a calendar-year AG, by 30 June; extensions are not granted beyond the mandatory six-month shareholders’-meeting window
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to hold the general assembly breaches the board’s fiduciary duty and can trigger a court-ordered convocation at board expense; defective shareholder records may invalidate shareholder resolutions and create personal civil liability of directors

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Share Register and Beneficial Owners (UBO) Confirmation Statement (shareholder roll, bearer-share UBO notation and current control declarations)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Kept at the registered office in Switzerland; available for inspection by Commercial Registry authorities, cantonal tax authorities, statutory auditors and Swiss financial intermediaries under anti-money-laundering verification
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Updated continuously upon each share transfer; the formal annual completeness confirmation is executed by the board between balance-sheet date and the Annual General Meeting
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Deficient share register and UBO documentation is a statutory infringement subject to public-law fines; unregistered or unmoted shareholders lose enforceability of their shareholder rights, and the AG may be barred from claiming exemptions in court

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: A Swiss AG is required to appoint an ordinary auditor if it is listed on a stock exchange, has qualifying bonds, or exceeds two of the following three thresholds in each of two consecutive fiscal years: total assets CHF 20 million; annual gross revenue CHF 40 million; annual average full-time employees 250. A limited statutory audit applies to non-exempt AGs, but an AG with fewer than 10 full-time employees may be fully exempted from independent audit by unanimous shareholders’ resolution.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Swiss statutory annual accounts must be prepared under the Swiss Code of Obligations (Art. 958–963), generally applied as Swiss GAAP FER; listed or group-reporting companies additionally prepare consolidated financial statements under IFRS or Swiss GAAP FER applying true-and-fair-view principles.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Switzerland maintains no central UBO register. Under Art. 697j–697l of the Code of Obligations, the AG must identify and record every natural person who ultimately owns or controls the company; each share transfer must be recorded in the Register of Members, and bearer-share beneficial owners must be disclosed before exercising voting rights. At each Annual General Meeting, the board reviews, signs, and dates the member register and UBO notes; these records must be retained at the Swiss registered office. Swiss financial intermediaries must collect a current UBO declaration before providing banking services, and tax and registry authorities have a statutory right of inspection.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Directors and Managing Officers
Minute Book of Shareholders’ General Assembly and Board of Directors
Commercial Correspondence and Accounting Files (business records)

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 1,800 – 4,500 per annum for a Swiss licensed domiciliation or registered-office service, including registered office access, governmental correspondence handling and regulatory mail forwarding in cantonal centres such as Zug, Zurich or Geneva; VAT excluded.
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 0 for a fully exempt micro AG (fewer than 10 employees and unanimous shareholders’ opt-out); USD 5,000 – 15,000 per annum for a limited statutory audit; USD 15,000 – 45,000 per annum for an ordinary audit of a mid-sized AG depending on complexity and IFRS or group-reporting requirements.

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: Federal direct corporate income tax: 8.5% on taxable net profit (equivalent to 7.83% on a pre-tax basis); combined federal, cantonal and communal headline range for an AG: 11.9% - 21.0%; Zug (Crypto Valley) combined rate approx. 11.9% - 12.2%.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: STAF/TAF 2020 reforms abolished privileged status regimes but introduced: (1) patent box deduction reducing up to 90% of qualifying IP income (AI models/LLM patents eligible); (2) R&D super-deduction of 50% on Swiss R&D costs; (3) notional interest deduction on surplus equity in most cantons; (4) participation deduction exempting 95% of qualifying dividend and capital gain income; (5) step-up and deferred liquidation relief for hidden reserves; an AI LLM API platform with Swiss IP ownership and Zug substance can achieve a combined effective rate of approx. 7.5% - 10% on patent-box-eligible income.
